今天在商店刷到的意外之喜，首发下单。久违的传统硬核塔防，关卡设计很用心，分量十足，不过技能 QTE 的设计有待商榷。它似乎既无益于策略，也无法成为调剂，带来更多的是没能完美触发时的挫败感。 PS. 感谢本地化，但中文字体有必要换成更常规的像素字体（或黑体），目前的 readbility 有些糟糕。

Fun tower defense, good amount of variety, unlocks and challenges. My only real complaint so far is that on the boss stages you have no method to pause and plan at all, if you pause it goes to a screen where you can't see the map or make changes so it takes away from the strategy aspect and turns it into an action response situation. Some people may like that, but it doesn't fit the rest of the stages where you get to plan between waves.

像是2D版的兽人必须死，玩着确实还挺有意思。因为这游戏攻略什么的还挺少，强推1-8给的大炮，贯通+不错的伤害+击退控制，打大型boss还有多段伤害相当无脑。用箱子或发生器（向日葵版箱子）把怪聚到一条路上，用大炮把路架住，，后续可以给路上铺泥坑减速，在出口位置放翻转板把冲出来的怪再重新推进泥坑吃大炮击退，只要能拐角架炮的关卡大炮都能给你不错的游戏体验，只需要注意一下破坏建筑的怪，提前布好翻转板推进悬崖或者技能豆怪收掉。

Overall Impression: B. An interesting town defense game that made me feel I got my money's worth. A tower defense game with enough unique twists to make it interesting. Some of the the challenges can be a little much, but most of them make you think in different ways on how to best use traps and the bean beasts. No bugs or glitches so far. There are some really tough levels, later on in the game. There is one that is downright frustrating where your towers will slide off the map. That one is not fun at all. The final boss is a trip. Bring your A game for that one.
I can't cheat and get one gem requirement done, then replay the level and get the other gem requirement done, and then have them both completed on the map. 10/10

The gameplay loop of having to progress stages for unlocks but then go back and replay stages when you have the unlocks that enable doing their challenges for gems to get any upgrades isn't fun at all. The progression design is too flawed by showing you can't full clear stages immediately thus forcing a lot of backtracking to replay boring stages. Either this was a lack of thoughtfulness or the dev aimed for intentionally playtime bloating systems.

[h1]《豆怪》：萌出血的硬核像素塔防[/h1] 《豆怪》无疑是部让人感到惊喜但又充满塔防的作品，惊喜在于游戏粗陋外表之下的高完成度，遗憾则是终究是因为卖相不佳导致惨淡开局，目前空有93%的好评率、但仅仅收获了不到100条评价——更何况游戏卖的也不贵，中文区55元的价格，对如今的独游市场来说已经是颇具性价比的选择了。 我比较喜欢本作的美术设计，精美的像素点阵组合搭配出多种多样的场景，从森林到雪地，从火山到洞穴，丰富的塔防场景保证了游戏的视觉呈现，并且在怪物设计上也颇费了番功夫，对不同种类的怪物都有详尽的刻画，关底BOSS也有专门的出场动画，在细节上已经尽力做到最好了。 但归根结底，像素游戏好像已经不再是市场上的热门——这条赛道实在是太卷了。以本作的像素精度，放到市场上也不是那种一眼就能出彩的种，所以泯然众人倒是可以理解。不过即便画面不算出彩，游戏在Gameplay上我觉得还是做的比较优秀的。 其核心玩法融合了两款热门塔防《王国保卫战》以及《兽人必须死》的核心设计，主要防御设施分为「豆怪」以及「陷阱」两种，并且都有各自的升级形态，能解锁出更强力的武器。游戏里包括10种豆怪跟12种陷阱，丰富度上已经满足塔防游戏的基本需求了，并且还设置了「主动技能」让玩家操作——你可以看做是KR里的英雄，只不过是站桩非移动版本。 《豆怪》在关卡策略上相当考究，颇有《王国保卫战》早年的风姿，高难度下必须要精打细算才能摸到过关的解法，而如果你是传说中的高高手，也有无尽模式在等着你去征服。 总而言之，《豆怪》是一部初看并不起眼、但实际完成度非常高的硬核塔防游戏，在软萌的像素外表之下，用可爱的豆怪们打造出最较劲脑汁的策略塔防游戏——真男人不是在杀敌，就是在杀敌的路上。喜欢塔防的你不要犹豫，冲就对了！ [quote]关注[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/36224058/]老实人鉴赏家 [/url] [url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/laoshirenLSR]老实人评测[/url]：独立游戏爱好者聚集地，黄油绅士交流中心。 不错过游戏的亮点，不放过游戏的槽点，带给玩家最直观的测评感受。[/quote]

实在要说的话，应该算作中评。游戏的质量还不错，4个大关，每个10关（含2个boss关）+2无尽关卡，内容算是充足了，像素风的美术风格也没法挑什么刺，问题在于其核心玩法塔防，但游玩的感觉完全不像是塔防，反而像是解密游戏。 以下内容含部分剧透 游戏中的小怪（尤其是后期）有大量免疫和抵抗的元素和状态类型，基本每关能带的塔没有太多的自由性，尤其是要做关卡任务和高难度通关（高难度下抵抗的伤害类型造成的伤害更少），所以玩起来没有塔防的自由度，反而像是把关卡里所有怪物不抵抗的伤害类型凑齐来通关。而且最**的一点是后面的怪抵抗类型这么重要还得先打几十个怪才能解锁怪物信息，这不就逼你初见去盲猜吗？这个解锁机制的意义在哪里？

[h1]可爱却硬核[/h1] 本作是一款看似画风休闲却实际上颇具难度的塔防游戏。流程上采用大区域+小关卡的模式推进，敌人会按波次和路径袭来。玩家主要的防御手段为可以进化培养的豆子、支持升级的陷阱（有些有朝向）以及可以主动释放的技能魔法，玩家还可以通过放置障碍物改变怪物的行径路线。虽然玩家也可以选择低难度进行游玩，但是支撑局外升级和内容解锁的商店，其所需的宝石与难度和挑战任务息息相关，还是比较考验玩家的策略搭配和操作水平的。 [quote]关注「 [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/42276832//]鸿源鉴游组」 [/url] [/quote] [u][b] 会当逢佳游，始可见鸿源。 [/b][/u]

Yes, [i]Bean Beasts[/i] is visually stunning and an appealing concept hypothetically, but its gameplay damns it to being second-rate. For players who welcome a challenge, this product subtly bars players from hard mode in the beginning through making enemies tankier, resistences stronger, and resources remaining the same which is to say that the game is already stingy and that players in the early stages will not have the [b]appropriate[/b] traps and bean beasts to effectively beat back the stronger hordes of enemies. There is a shop system that consumes gems to unlock upgrades and utilities, but gems can only be unlocked through rather stressful challenges and higher difficulties, which means progress is locked behind having to either redo levels for gems, as later levels will not let up on players if they do not have certain trap combos or upgrades that make selling and repositioning traps less burdensome. The lesson to be learned here is that progression should at no point rely on forcing players to redo levels to unlock utilities and upgrades when harder difficulties yield little rewards in a game that is already ungenerous in giving players resources. This artificially lengthens the game and makes what could have been an impressive $7 tower defense video game into a $14 stock pixel game.

It is an interesting take on the TD formula, but it's still the same old "Beat it this way, to win!" nonsense that has always plagued most TD's. The fun is in the "finding out" how the Developer intended for you to beat the level but that is also part of the rub. Which is why the game allows you to replay the wave over and over trying minor adjustments to your setup. The Shop towers are mostly well... rubbish. They are not better than your current towers and the Ballista is consistently the best tower meaning to win the game you don't get to use the towers you like as much as you would like. The "leveling" is also a bit... well nonsense. They level up by shooting which means putting them in a well placed spot for maximum effectiveness for their attack type will also mean it does not get to level up unless you spend beans. Again, it's all about how the Dev designed the level to be beat. It's not as fun as Defenders Quest, they did the leveling of units RIGHT and it's a real shame others have not figured out how to do this well despite having a good example. I had fun for 6 hours... I do plan to return to it later to see how it's development has gone, but it looks like another "fun up front" but "annoying at the endgame" TD.

It has it's strong points but ultimately it's not that fun to play. Progression just becomes too tedious even early in the game. Levels already feel too much of the same and then you're forced to redo levels and do bothersome challenges to get more upgrades. The towers lack variety, there aren't enough different possible strategies to beat a stage and the stages themselves aren't dynamic. If the definition of a game is a series of interesting choices then Bean Beast just doesn't have enough choices to make.
Just starting and the game feels great. Looking forward to seeing how it plays as I progress into the harder levels!

Brilliant tower defence game and honestly a steal for the price. Pros: -adorable pixel art -fun strategic puzzles -very catchy and well made OST -well utilized tower loadout, very few redundancies -cool boss fights with interesting twist mechanics that make you think on your feet -branching upgrades and buffs -meta progression -goldfish cons: -low stakes losses, restarting the wave is always an option, so losing isn't really punished. -ability value seems to vary wildly -boss fights can be a bit hectic and are somewhat of a tonal shift compared to the gameplay loop of rest of the game in my opinion. Still really like them, but I can see why some wouldn't -why the is that robo tower so OP lmao

Overall, this game was a good entertainment, although the late game was that awful that I simply stopped playing. The game provides a lot of interesting choices and twists to a genre that struggle to evolve, like choosing your turrets and beats/guardian/spells loadouts, or enemies that can break the maze, entire boss fights with short cd on all spells. Each region offers a unique set of monsters and each map a unique roster based on the region set, with their own weaknesses and resistances, meaning you have to adapt your loadout to match those. In other words, you can't just play "the best combo" each and every time, which is cool I think. It's also kind of pretty for a pixel art game. Also I love the plate trap :D Now, every mission has 3 missions that are mandatory in order to unlock stuff, interesting, but some of them are very lame like breaking a damage sponge, sorry, a chest. Another one asks you to break that damn chest before turn x. Furthermore, late game missions are too exhausting and some are unbalanced like the one with moving walls, cool idea but poorly executed. Personal note: 6/10.
